tagline.text: White sand and cobalt-blue sea at the northern tip of Luzon

image.credit: Sindre Helvik / CC BY 3.0 / Wikimedia Commons

items.credit: Perry A. Dominguez / CC BY-SA 3.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: Known as the "Boracay of the North," Pagudpud is a beach town at the very northern tip of Luzon. From the fine white sands of Saud Beach to Blue Lagoon, a favorite with surfers, to Kabigan Falls hidden in the jungle and the cliff-hugging Patapat Viaduct, it offers a quiet, laid-back getaway.
Pagudpud sits at the very northern edge of Ilocos Norte province, at the northern tip of Luzon. It's a long haul, over
2 hours

up the coast road from Laoag, but the sea waiting at the end of that drive is worth it. Saud Beach, its fine white sand curving like a crescent moon, deepens from a transparent turquoise near shore to a deep cobalt farther out, which is why it has long been nicknamed the "Boracay of the North."

What sets it apart from Boracay is how quiet it is. Rather than a resort town lined with big hotels and nightlife, this is a peaceful coast dotted with beach resorts under the shade of palm trees. Outside weekends and peak season, you can practically have a stretch of beach to yourself, and at night only the sound of the waves and the stars remain.
The sea isn't all there is, either. Walk about
30 minutes
into the jungle and you'll find Kabigan Falls, over

high, and the Patapat Viaduct, which winds along cliffs above the South China Sea, is one of the Philippines' most celebrated drives. In winter, surfers flock to Blue Lagoon to ride the waves whipped up by the northeast monsoon.

It suits families and couples who want to relax by the sea while adding a bit of waterfall trekking and driving. Since the trip from Laoag is long for a day visit, staying at least one night and touring northern Ilocos together with the Bangui Windmills and Kapurpurawan Rock Formation is recommended.

Pagudpud's flagship beach has fine sand and a gentle slope, making it good for playing in the water with kids. The sea is calm and clear during the dry season, but waves rise on windy days, so check the flags on-site.

East of Saud Beach, Blue Lagoon lives up to its name with beautiful blue water, and the two rock islets known as "Dos Hermanos" out at sea add a scenic focal point. The wide beach is great for walking and photography.
When the northeast monsoon blows from around
November
to
March
, good surfing waves roll into Blue Lagoon. You can rent a board and take a beginner lesson at the surf shops on the beach.
From the entrance, a walk of about
30 minutes
along rice paddies and a forest trail leads to a waterfall about
high with a cold pool beneath it. You register at the ranger station and go in with a local guide.
This viaduct runs about
1.3 km
along the sea cliffs east of Pagudpud, with jungle cliffs on one side and the South China Sea spread out on the other. It's a good spot to pull over at a roadside viewpoint and take photos.
A small roadside spring and shrine near the Patapat Viaduct, said to bring good fortune to those who drink its water. The cold, clear spring water is a refreshing way to beat the heat for a moment.

A distinctive rock formation with a hole running through the middle of a seaside hill; its name means "mountain with a hole" in Ilocano. Climbing the steps to the view of the sea through the hole is striking.

children.text: Saud Beach faces northwest, giving it beautiful sunset colors, and with few village lights around, the stars come out in force on clear nights.

The best time for swimming is from

Lodging is concentrated in two areas, Saud Beach and Blue Lagoon. Saud Beach has fine sand and is close to restaurants and amenities, making it convenient for families visiting for the first time, with beachfront resort rooms priced around

per night. Blue Lagoon has a wider, quieter beach, home to Hannah's Beach Resort, a long-established large property, along with mid-range resorts and budget lodging for surfers. Guesthouses along the town and roadside go for around
per night.

Most meals are had at resort restaurants. Bagnet and pinakbet, the classic Ilocano dishes, along with fish and squid grilled over charcoal that day, and shrimp sinigang (a tangy soup), are the staples. Small beachside eateries sell fresh coconut juice and halo-halo, while the town market offers cheap local meals. Pagudpud also does seafood cured in coconut vinegar well, so a seafood dinner with kilawin (vinegar-cured ceviche) is a popular choice.
Pagudpud has very few ATMs, and cash withdrawal often fails. Bring enough cash from Laoag to cover your expenses beyond accommodation.
Some resorts don't accept card payments. Check the payment method when you book.
Phone signal reaches most beach resorts, but weakens near the falls and along the Patapat stretch.
The path to Kabigan Falls crosses rice paddies and streams, so aqua shoes or trekking sandals are comfortable.
Saud Beach photos come out with the clearest water color in the morning light. Blue Lagoon is beautiful at sunset with the Dos Hermanos rock islets in silhouette.
The last bus from Laoag to Pagudpud often stops running in the late afternoon. On your return day, depart before
Resorts fill up early during Holy Week and the
May
and
December
holidays. Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance.
Beach trash bins can be scarce, so it's a good idea to bring a small trash bag and take your own litter with you.
At Saud Beach there is a Tourist Rest Area opened by the Department of Tourism in
May 2024
. It has restrooms and tourist information facilities, making it a good place to rest for a while during a northern tour.
During the strong northeast monsoon from
November to February
, waves and rip currents get stronger. Avoid swimming on beaches without a lifeguard, and never go in when a red flag is up.
Kabigan Falls is closed when water levels rise during the rainy season. The rocks below the falls are slippery, so don't attempt reckless dives.
During typhoon season, there is a risk of falling rocks and landslides around the Patapat Viaduct. Follow any traffic control notices.
Confirm the fare and what's included in advance for tricycle tours and surf lessons.
The sun is very strong. Reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard are recommended.
Most Pagudpud beaches have no lifeguard on duty. On days with high waves, staying no deeper than ankle level is the safest choice.
